fields.description: Fix the database export recipe to use the renamed task_deps table.
fields.context: Causes 'no such table' error on export.

fields.title: Add --watch auto-restart flag to endless serve
fields.description: Add a --watch flag to endless serve that restarts the server gracefully when its binary is updated.
fields.analysis: Add graceful shutdown support as prerequisite.

fields.title: Accept prefixed task IDs everywhere in the CLI
fields.description: Accept both raw numbers and prefixed task IDs in every CLI flag and argument that takes a task ID.
fields.context: Currently --parent and possibly others only accept integers.

fields.description: Add a tier to tasks (auto, quick, deep, discuss) classifying how autonomously they can be done, settable and filterable with a --tier flag.
fields.analysis: 1=auto, 2=quick, 3=deep, 4=discuss. Add --tier flag to task add/update/list/next. Supports both numeric and label input.

fields.description: Add a declined task status with a decline command that requires a reason, and an outcome field on tasks that can be set at completion.
fields.analysis: Add 'task decline <id> --reason <text>' command (reason required). Add optional '--outcome <text>' to 'task complete'. Add '--outcome' flag to 'task show'.

fields.description: Improve table-recreate migrations so they tolerate stale temp tables left by a prior run and conflicts with concurrent sessions.
fields.analysis: Add DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before CREATE, and consider handling concurrent session conflicts gracefully.

fields.description: Design a strategy for detecting and gracefully handling conflicts when multiple sessions modify the database at once.
Evaluate whether task remove needs soft-delete for undo and audit, or whether declined status plus hard delete of junk is enough.
fields.context: Currently task remove does a hard DELETE.

fields.description: Fix the task next and task recent queries to select the tier, so their tables can show it.
fields.notes: Added t.tier to both queries.

fields.title: Fix task next to order by phase, status, then tier
fields.description: Fix task next to order by phase, then status, then tier, then recency, and leave in-progress and verify tasks out of its results.
fields.context: Current ordering is status > phase > updated_at.
fields.analysis: Also remove in_progress and verify from next results — those belong in task active.

fields.description: Add a task active command listing in-progress and verify tasks, the work you are currently responsible for.
fields.analysis: Separates 'what am I working on' (active) from 'what should I pick up' (next).

fields.description: Update the web dashboard backlog to use the same sort order as task next.
fields.notes:
Once CLI task next ordering is settled (phase > status > tier),

Hold off until CLI ordering is verified.

fields.description: Fix the task detail pane metadata to list ID first, show tier, and color labels dimmer than values, matching the CLI's style.

fields.title: Add CHECK constraint tying completed_at to completed status
fields.description: Add a constraint to the tasks table so a completion time can only be set when status is completed.
Change the default task list output from the tree to a flat table sorted by ID, with a --tree flag for the tree view.
fields.analysis: Add --tree flag to optionally show the current tree view.

fields.description: Migrate Endless to an event-sourced architecture with per-project event logs and SQLite as a rebuildable projection, in stages.
fields.analysis:
# Where the rebuild work moved (2026-08-25)

This epic held the April five-stage design. The rebuild-reliability half of it
is owned by **E-1935**, filed in August for exactly that, and the measured state
of `rebuild-db --confirm` — the full transitive FK closure, the four gaps and
their owners, and the ordering constraint on `sessions.task_id` — lives in
E-1935's analysis rather than being duplicated here.

E-1041, E-2062 and E-1728 moved to E-1935 with it. E-894 and its subtree moved
to E-1486, the port epic, being port work rather than event-sourcing work.

What remains here is the design-stage work: E-806, E-809, E-810, E-813, E-814,
E-816, E-817, plus E-910 and E-914.

## From the description

Per-project .endless/events.jsonl + global changelog repo, with SQLite as rebuildable projection. 5-stage migration.

fields.description: Generate Markdown files on disk from ledger content, and keep them in sync, when an external tool Endless works alongside requires them.
fields.notes:
Parked.

Revive against a concrete external tool, which will specify the requirement better than this placeholder.
fields.analysis: Generation and sync only — the event-sourced document entity this epic originally proposed is obsolete, since brainstorm tasks took over the evolving-design role documents were meant to fill.

fields.description: Implement a Go package that serializes hybrid logical clock timestamps as strings that sort lexicographically and stay human-readable.
fields.analysis:
Go package at internal/kairos/.

Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.SSSSSS-XXXX-NNN. Node ID per-installation stored in ~/.config/endless/node_id. Build inside Endless, extract as standalone package later.

fields.description: Define the fixed event envelope and the initial closed set of task, dependency, session, and project event kinds, stored in per-machine segment files.
fields.analysis:
Line-delimited JSON. Initial task/dep/session/project event kinds including revisit status and tags. Events stored in segmented files per node: .endless/events/events-{node_id}-{seq}.jsonl.

Each machine writes only to its own segments; git merge adds files, never line conflicts.

fields.description: Implement Go subcommands that append events to per-machine segment files, with the Python CLI calling them while the database stays authoritative.
fields.analysis:
Python CLI shells out to Go for all event writes — single implementation, no format divergence. Writes to .endless/events/events-{node_id}-{seq}.jsonl. Rotation when segment exceeds threshold.

DB remains authoritative in Stage 1.

Enables sqlc from day one.

fields.description: Make the user config directory optionally a git repo holding cross-project events, synced across machines with git pull and push.
fields.analysis:
No separate changelog repo.

Cross-project events (project registered, cross-project deps) go here. .gitignore excludes endless.db (rebuildable projection) and local cache files. Multi-machine sync via git pull/push in this directory.

fields.description: Build a deterministic projection engine and a rebuild command that recreate the SQLite database from event logs, validated against the current database.
fields.analysis:
Given same events, any machine produces same DB state.

Implement endless rebuild-db.

Validate projection matches current DB.

fields.title: Make event logs authoritative over SQLite
fields.description: Make event logs authoritative: every write goes through the Go event writer first, and SQLite becomes a cache updated by projection.
fields.analysis: Projection updates SQLite incrementally as side effect. Python CLI is fully dependent on Go for writes. DB becomes a cache. endless rebuild-db supported for disaster recovery.

fields.description: Implement a compact command that merges old event segments into a local, uncommitted state file for faster replay.
fields.analysis:
Local-only operation, not committed to git.

Never modifies git-committed segment files. Old segments optionally prunable after checkpoint, but that's a future optimization.

fields.description: Migrate task ordering from integer sort order to lexicographic rank strings, so a task can be inserted between two others without renumbering.
fields.analysis:
Use morikuni/go-lexorank.

Insertion between two tasks without renumbering.

Background rebalance pass.

fields.description: Refactor the catch-all task text field into separate plan, acceptance, design, and notes fields, moving existing text into plan.
fields.analysis: Each gets own event kind. Migration: existing text → plan field, others empty.

fields.title: Implement typed task dependency model
fields.description: Implement a task dependency model with blocks, parent-child and related types, including cross-project dependencies, and use its graph when task next picks work.
fields.analysis: dep.created/dep.removed events. Cross-project deps via global ID. Dependency graph in projection. endless task next uses graph + tier + phase + status.

fields.title: Implement close-time gates for task completion
fields.description: Implement pluggable close-time gates, such as file exists, tests pass, branch merged, children closed and human verified, that block closing a task with a clear error.
fields.analysis: Gates block close with clear error.

fields.title: Handle multi-agent write conflicts
fields.description: Handle conflicting writes from concurrent agents by resolving them deterministically at projection time, parking invariant violations as conflict records, and surfacing those for resolution.
fields.notes: Consolidates E-815.
fields.context: Concurrent agents can write conflicting state.

fields.description: Implement a workflow that parks invariant violations as conflict records, surfaces them in the dashboard, CLI and MCP, and resolves each with a new event.
fields.analysis: Surface in dashboard. Expose via CLI + MCP. AI proposes resolution or escalates. Resolution is a new event.

fields.title: Implement paired local and global task identifiers
fields.description: Implement paired task identifiers: a short local ID for humans and a content-hash global ID for machines, mapped one-to-one, with cross-repo dependencies using the global ID.
fields.analysis: E-47 for humans, SHA-256 prefix for machines. 1:1 mapping in projection. Cross-repo deps use global ID.

fields.title: Build a hook adaptor layer decoupled from Claude Code
fields.description: Build Endless's own hook vocabulary plus a Claude Code adaptor that translates into it, opening the way to adaptors for other agent tools.
fields.analysis:
Claude-Code-specific adaptor translates.

Opens path to Codex/Cursor/Gemini adaptors.

fields.title: Implement an import-only Beads backend
fields.description: Implement an import-only Beads backend that imports all Beads tasks into Endless as events by shelling out to the bd CLI.
fields.analysis:
Shell out to bd --json. Import all tasks via bd list. Emit task.imported_from_backend events.

Optional history synthesis from git log of issues.jsonl.

fields.description: Add two-way sync for the Beads backend: push compatible events out, pull changes in with loop prevention, and queue offline changes for retry.
fields.analysis: Outbound push of compatible events. Inbound pull with loop prevention via endless_origin correlation token. Offline queue with retry.

fields.title: Show backend sync degradation in the dashboard
fields.description: Show in the dashboard which data is Endless-only versus synced to a backend, with status overlays and reports of what did not sync.

fields.title: Design a document entity schema with ordered sections
fields.description: Design a document entity schema with stable identifiers, whose sections also have stable identifiers and sortable string positions for ordering.
fields.analysis: Stable local_id + global_id. Sections with stable identifiers, Lexorank positions. documents + document_sections tables in projection.

fields.description: Implement events for creating, editing, moving and archiving documents and their sections, and a projection that builds each document with ordered sections.
fields.analysis:
doc.created, doc.section_added/updated/renamed/moved/removed, doc.archived.

Cached in SQLite.

fields.title: Build a review step for regenerated document sections
fields.description: Build a review step for document regeneration: stage proposed section replacements without applying them, show the diff, then apply on accept or keep the original on decline.
fields.analysis:
doc.section_replacement_proposed stages content without applying. Dashboard shows diff. Accept → doc.section_updated. Decline → original preserved.

Mirrors verify/declined.

fields.title: Surface conflicting concurrent edits to document sections
fields.description: Surface concurrent edits to the same document section for three-way merge review, and structural conflicts such as delete versus update as pending items.
fields.analysis:
Structural conflicts (delete vs update) as pending items.

Same pattern as task conflicts.

fields.description: Build the endless doc commands to add and show documents, add and update sections, apply from a file, and view history, with idempotent machine-parseable output.
fields.analysis: Idempotent, machine-parseable output for Claude Code sessions.

fields.title: Build a command to apply chat-edited markdown to a doc
fields.description: Build endless doc apply-from-chat, which compares a markdown file to the current document and records section-level changes for the differences.
fields.context: Medium-term Claude web bridge.
fields.analysis: ~few hundred lines of Go.

fields.description: Add MCP tools to list documents, read a document or section, propose section updates or replacements, and add or remove sections.
fields.analysis: Narrower than CLI to steer AI toward section-level ops.

fields.title: Add document import from markdown files
fields.description: Add an endless doc import command that parses a markdown file into a document with one section per heading.
fields.analysis: Parse markdown, create doc entity, emit section events per header. Configurable: rendered file vs Endless-only.

fields.description: Omit declined tasks, like completed ones, from task list's default output, showing them only with --all.
fields.notes: Now excludes both unless --all is used.

fields.description: Add a --phase flag to task update so a task's phase can be changed after creation.
fields.context: Phase can be set at creation (task add --phase) but cannot be changed after.

fields.title: Let channel connect auto-detect the active beacon
fields.description: Let endless channel connect run with no arguments and auto-detect the project's active beacon, requiring an ID only when several exist, with clearer not-found errors.
fields.context:
When a session runs 'endless channel beacon', the instructions tell other sessions to run 'endless channel connect <id>'.

The hex ID is easy to mis-copy.
fields.analysis:
Changes: (1) Beacon output should show the channel ID on its own line but simplify the connect instruction to just 'endless channel connect' (no args).

Only require an ID when multiple beacons exist. (3) Improve error message to distinguish 'not found' from 'not in beacon state'.

fields.title: Design ADRs as a document type
fields.description: Design architecture decision records as a document type with standard sections (context, decision, consequences, status), task references and the proposal and review workflow.
fields.context: ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) are a natural document type.

fields.title: Validate titles passed to task update --title
fields.description: Validate that titles passed to task update --title start with a registered verb, rejecting any that do not.
fields.notes: Already implemented — validate_title() is called in update_plan() at line 1204 of task_cmd.py.
fields.context: Verified: 'endless task update E-842 --title "broken title"' correctly rejects non-verb starts.

fields.title: Allow multiple values in the task list --status filter
fields.description: Allow the task list --status filter to accept comma-separated values, such as needs_plan,ready,in_progress.
fields.context: Currently only accepts a single value.

fields.title: Fix hook errors to always exit non-zero
fields.description: Fix hook error handling so every failure, including session tracking and activity recording, exits non-zero and Claude stops to show the user instead of silently continuing.
fields.context:
E-708 incorrectly classified session tracking, activity recording, and other DB operations as 'non-fatal' (log to stderr but continue).

The original bug that triggered E-708 was exactly this kind of 'non-fatal' error causing lost data.
fields.analysis: The user must approve any bypass — the AI must not silently degrade.

fields.title: Record hook and channel errors in log files
fields.description: Record hook and channel errors in log files under the Endless config directory as well as on stderr.
fields.notes:
Implemented as part of E-844 —

hook and channel errors now log to ~/.config/endless/log/hook.log and channel.log respectively, using io.MultiWriter for both stderr and file output.

fields.description: Add an assumed status for tasks believed complete but not yet verified, and rename the completed status to confirmed across the codebase.
fields.analysis: Pre-1.0 with no external users, so clean break.

fields.title: Allow multiple task IDs on single-task commands
fields.description: Allow commands that take one task ID, such as update, show, start and move, to accept several IDs and apply the same operation to each.
fields.analysis:
Covers: task update, task confirm, task assume, task remove, task start, task show, task move.

Example: 'endless task assume E-708 E-730 E-739'.

fields.title: Add --blocked-by flag to task update
fields.description: Add a --blocked-by flag to task update that records which task blocks this one when setting it blocked, queryable by the blocking task.
fields.notes: Note: E-812 (full dependency model) might obsolete this, but it's useful now before that lands.
fields.analysis: Stores the blocking task ID as metadata. Queryable so we can answer 'what's blocked by E-799'.

fields.title: Add integration tests for Beads JSON output
fields.description: Add integration tests that check the JSON structure the Beads bd CLI outputs, so breaking changes in it are caught early.
fields.context: bd CLI output format is not under our control.

fields.title: Build document list and detail views in the dashboard
fields.description: Build a document list in the dashboard project view and a detail view with rendered sections, edit history, and pending proposals and conflicts to accept or decline.
fields.analysis: Read-centric with accept/decline controls.

fields.title: Implement basic task dependency tracking in the CLI
fields.description: Implement lightweight CLI commands to record which tasks block which, list a task's dependencies, show blockers in task show, and filter task list by blocked or blocking.
fields.notes:
before E-812 lands the full event-sourced model.

E-812 will replace this but the data can migrate.
fields.analysis: Uses existing task_deps table. Commands: endless task block <id> --by <id>, endless task deps <id>. Show blockers in task show output. Filter: endless task list --blocked, --blocking.

fields.description: Show a task's blocked-by and blocking dependencies in the web dashboard detail pane, matching task show in the CLI.
fields.context: CLI now shows blocked-by and blocking in task show output.

fields.title: Add an obsolete status for overtaken tasks
fields.description: Add an obsolete status, distinct from declined, for tasks made irrelevant by other changes rather than actively rejected.
fields.context: Needed for tasks like E-714 that were superseded.
fields.analysis: Declined = active decision not to do. Obsolete = passively made irrelevant by other changes.

fields.title: Make tier 1 tasks start ready, never needing a plan
fields.description: Make tier 1 (automatic) tasks unable to have needs_plan status: enforce it in the schema, set ready automatically on add, and fix existing data.
fields.analysis: Tier 1 (auto) tasks cannot have needs_plan status — they don't need a plan by definition.

fields.description: Clear a task's tier to n/a when it reaches verify, confirmed, assumed, declined or obsolete, and keep --tier none matching only untriaged tasks.
fields.context: Prevents stale tier labels on finished tasks.
fields.analysis: Tier 0 displays as 'n/a'. --tier none filters for NULL only (untriaged), not 0.

fields.title: Build session conversation history
fields.description: Build capture of session conversation content using hooks, with CLI commands to list, show and reimport history and a web page showing each session's messages.
fields.analysis: CLI: session history, session list, session reimport. Web: /sessions/<id> with reverse-chron, collapsed tools, lazy loading.

fields.description: Capture images referenced in session transcripts by copying them into the project's .endless/images before their temp files disappear, and clean up old ones.
fields.context: Images in transcripts reference temp files that get cleaned up.
fields.analysis: Add cleanup for images older than N days.

fields.title: Add a live session viewer command
fields.description: Add endless session watch, which continuously shows a session's new messages as they arrive, like tail -f, for use in a pane beside Claude.
fields.context: Run in a tmux pane alongside Claude for real-time conversation review. Similar to claude-history's continuous sync but integrated with Endless.

fields.title: Generate session recaps in the background
fields.description: Generate per-session recap summaries from Claude Code transcripts in the background, refreshing each after a number of new user messages.

fields.title: Add a --text flag to task add
fields.description: Add a --text flag to endless task add that sets the task's body from a file at creation, as task update already can.
fields.context: endless task add only takes --description (short string); body-from-file requires a separate task update --text call.

fields.description: Split database migrations into automatic additive ones and table rebuilds that run only via an explicit endless db migrate, which backs up the database first.
fields.context: Fixes chronic data loss from rebuild migrations running on every hook fire.
fields.analysis: Automatic migrations: only ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, UPDATE, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. Table rebuilds (CHECK changes, column drops) require explicit 'endless db migrate' with auto-backup of DB file first.

fields.description: Implement one schema-versioned migration runner that applies migrations only when the database version is behind, with an explicit migrate command that backs up first.
fields.notes: Distribution (E-716) depends on this —
fields.analysis:
(1) _schema_version table with single integer, (2) one migration runner (not both Go and Python), (3) migrations run only when version is behind, (4) 'endless db migrate' command with auto-backup, (5) no table rebuilds in auto-migration.

shipping without proper migrations risks corrupting user databases.

fields.description: Add a --limit option to task search, matching task next and session search.
fields.context: Got 'No such option: --limit' when trying 'endless task search migration --limit 10'.
fields.analysis: Should match the pattern used by task next and session search.

fields.title: Add a busy timeout to all SQLite connections
fields.description: Add a busy timeout to every Go and Python SQLite connection so concurrent hook processes wait for a lock instead of failing immediately.
fields.analysis: Add PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000 to both Go (monitor/db.go) and Python (db.py) DB connections.

fields.description: Add a zsh/bash prompt hook that finds sessions needing a recap and runs endless session recap for them in the background.
fields.analysis: Also: session list inline fallback generates one recap per call for the most stale flagged session.

fields.title: Hide sessions created by recap generation
fields.description: Hide the sessions that endless session recap creates by calling claude -p, so they don't clutter the session list.
fields.context:
Each 'endless session recap' call creates a new session via claude -p hooks.

These clutter the session list.
fields.analysis: Options: auto-hide sessions with <= 2 messages in ended state, or find a way to run claude -p without triggering Endless hooks.

fields.description: Design how sessions recorded under a project's old directory names get mapped to the current project after it is renamed.
fields.context:
Projects get renamed (h2s → h24p → h2pp). Claude's JSONL paths encode the old name, so sessions from old names need to map to the current project.

Impacts session import, project reconciliation, and dashboard.
fields.analysis: Need to discuss: alias table? Rename history? Auto-detect from git remote? Heuristic matching?

fields.title: Hide error sessions at ingestion time
fields.description: Hide sessions whose summary is an error, such as 'Not logged in', when they are ingested, not only when they are displayed.
fields.notes: Sessions with error summaries like 'Not logged in' are now auto-hidden at ingestion time in both Go transcript parser and Python reimport. Previously only filtered at display time.

fields.description: Migrate session recap generation from Python to Go so the prompt hook can trigger it natively without shelling out to Python.
fields.context: Session recap (endless session recap) is currently Python-only, calling claude -p via subprocess.
fields.analysis: The Go version goes in internal/monitor/ or cmd/endless-hook/.

fields.description: Fix the hook failing in unregistered project directories, either by auto-registering the project or by failing with clear instructions to register it.
fields.context: ensureAnonymousProject uses status='anonymous' which is not in the CHECK constraint.
fields.analysis: Options: (1) auto-register as active with inferred metadata, (2) fail with clear instructions to run 'endless register'. Need to decide which behavior is correct.

fields.description: Add a --phase filter to task next, consistent with task list.
fields.context: task list has it.
fields.analysis: Should be consistent.

fields.description: Fix the go.mod replace directive to point at a public fork URL instead of a local path, so the Go session recap builds outside one developer's checkout.
fields.notes: Required before E-870 can be merged or used by other developers.
fields.context: so the Python-to-Go session-recap migration in parent E-870 builds successfully outside Mike's local checkout.

fields.title: Fix dependency display in task show
fields.description: Fix task show to label resolved blockers 'Enabled by' instead of 'Blocked by', and to keep its labels aligned when dependency labels are long.

fields.title: Document blocking semantics of verify and assumed
fields.description: Document in the session guide that tasks in verify still block their dependents while assumed tasks unblock them.
fields.analysis: This means when the only way to test a dependency is to implement the dependent task, change the blocker from verify to assumed.

fields.description: Add the date and time to the server's 'Binary changed, restarting' message so the user knows when the restart happened.
Add a backup of the database file on every hook invocation, as a temporary safety net until the cause of silent data corruption is fixed.
fields.context: Silent data corruption wiped all parent_id values from tasks.
fields.analysis: Temporary safety net.

fields.title: Fix status dropdown wrapping and double-click conflict
fields.description: Fix the status dropdown so its items stay on one line, and so double-clicking the status sphere no longer fires a single-click that toggles the detail pane.
fields.analysis:
Add whitespace-nowrap.

Need to suppress single-click when double-click detected.

fields.title: Move status dropdown to the detail pane status value
fields.description: Move the status dropdown trigger from double-clicking the status sphere to clicking the status value in the detail pane, removing the click-delay workaround.
fields.analysis:
Remove double-click and click-delay hack from status sphere.

Simpler, no latency, intuitive.

fields.title: Document web UI contrast and label/value rules
fields.description: Document the web UI's contrast and label color rules, such as a minimum text gray on dark backgrounds and distinct label colors, as a design standard.
fields.context: Established rules from multiple iterations: gray-400 minimum text on dark backgrounds, labels must use distinct color (emerald/cyan) not gray, context-appropriate child status summaries (needs-attention section only shows verify/blocked counts).

fields.description: Design a structured way to record development decisions with context, options and rationale, and to query them from the CLI and web.
fields.notes: Related to E-733 (ADR system) and E-801 (documents).
fields.context: Currently captured ad-hoc in task text fields, plan files, or not at all.
fields.analysis: Could be a document type, a task field, or a separate entity.

fields.title: Design automatic recording of changes and decisions
fields.description: Design hooks that automatically detect code changes without a task, flag unrecorded decisions, and ask for justification on status changes, so the system enforces recording.
fields.context:
Mike constantly has to remind Claude to record tasks, decisions, and justifications.

Goal: the system enforces recording, not the human.

fields.description: Hide the child status summary in the needs-attention section's compact rows, since it counted all active children rather than only those needing attention.
fields.notes: PROCESS LESSON: Claude initially substituted hiding for filtering (Mike's actual ask) without discussion. Mike's objection was process, not outcome — when Claude believes a different approach is better, Claude must explain trade-offs and let Mike choose, not silently substitute. Required form: 'I think X is better because Y — what do you think?' not '[ships X]'.
fields.context: The summary counted ALL active children, not just attention-needing ones, making '1 plan' misleading when only 1 child needed attention.
fields.analysis: Decision: hide entirely (vs. filter to verify/blocked) because needs-attention is expanded by default, making the summary redundant. Trade-off: loses 'at a glance' value if multiple attention-needing children exist; revisit if needs-attention becomes collapsed by default.

fields.title: Design lightweight queryable decision records
fields.description: Design a lightweight decision record type, listable and searchable, so design trade-offs raised in dialog have a first-class home instead of being buried in task descriptions.
fields.context:
Mike noticed that important design decisions and trade-offs surface during dialog (e.g. E-885 child summary debate) but have no first-class home in Endless.

Today they get buried in task descriptions or lost.
fields.analysis:
Should be lightweight — not full ADR ceremony — but queryable so past trade-offs can inform future choices.

Open questions: scope (per-task, per-project, cross-project?); structure (problem/options/resolution/why?); discovery (how surfaced when relevant?); whether to retroactively migrate decisions from existing task descriptions.

fields.title: Enforce recording of code changes and decisions
fields.description: Enforce recording with hooks that detect code edits without a task update, or decision-shaped dialog without a decision record, and either record them or block completion.
fields.context: Mike repeatedly has to remind Claude to record code changes as Endless tasks and decisions in a queryable place. This is a process leak: the assistant should not require user babysitting for recording.
fields.analysis: Open questions: detection signal (file edit + no task referenced? trigger phrases? heuristics?); intervention mode (auto-create task, prompt Claude, block exit?); false-positive cost (don't make trivial fixes ceremonial); interaction with E-886 decision capture.

fields.title: Make past decisions queryable as a class
fields.description: Make past decisions, especially design trade-offs, queryable as a class, so one command can list every architectural decision made about a topic.
fields.context:
Decisions made during work (especially design trade-offs) currently live in task descriptions, commit messages, and ad-hoc post-mortem docs. They are not queryable as a class.

Origin: emerged from E-885 post-mortem on 2026-04-25 where Mike noted 'ADRs can come out of these kinds of things.'
fields.analysis:
a dedicated 'decision' item type?

A tag/flag on tasks marking them as containing a decision? A separate 'endless decision list' command that pulls decisions from tasks/commits?

Goal: 'show me every architectural decision we've made about the status page' should be a single command.

fields.title: Add hooks to auto-record decisions and changes
fields.description: Add hooks that prompt Claude to record what changed and why after edits, warn on code changes without a task, and summarize decisions for capture at conversation end.
fields.context:
Mike repeatedly has to remind Claude to record changes, decisions, and justifications as Endless tasks/updates. This is a process-failure pattern that hooks could fix.

Origin: surfaced from E-885 post-mortem on 2026-04-25.
fields.analysis: Goal: Mike never has to say 'did you record that?' because the harness enforces it.

fields.title: Add a replaces relationship between tasks
fields.description: Add a replaces relationship between tasks that marks the replaced task obsolete and shows 'Replaced by' in task show.
fields.analysis: 'endless task replace E-750 --by E-880' creates the relationship and sets E-750 to obsolete. task show displays 'Replaced by: E-880'. Requires adding 'replaces' to the dep_type CHECK constraint or removing the CHECK and validating in application code.

fields.description: Remove all CHECK constraints from the SQLite schema and validate values in application code instead, doing one careful table rebuild with backups active.
fields.context: CHECK constraints in SQLite cannot be modified without rebuilding the entire table, which caused catastrophic data loss.
fields.analysis: One careful manual rebuild with backup system active.

fields.title: Consolidate Go binaries into one endless-go CLI
fields.description: Consolidate the separate serve, hook, channel and event Go binaries into a single endless-go binary with subcommands.
fields.analysis: Natural migration path as more CLI moves from Python to Go.

fields.title: Emit events for mutations the projection must rebuild
fields.description: Emit ledger events for mutations outside the task and decision domains so rebuild-db can restore every table the projection holds, after agreeing which entities still apply.
fields.notes: Consolidates E-911 and E-912;
fields.context: Mutations outside the task and decision domains never reach the ledger, so the projection cannot rebuild the tables that hold them and `rebuild-db` restores only tasks, decisions and decision_relations.
fields.analysis:
Consolidated 2026-08-25 from three tasks that carried the same sentence — 'Required before projection can rebuild <table>'.

E-910 (sessions): work_started, chat_started, idled, ended, task_completed,
recapped, hidden.
E-911 (projects): registered, updated, renamed, unregistered, purged.
E-912 (notes, conversations, messages): the remaining entity mutations.

Evidence for the scope call, NOT a scope decision — settle it against the tree
at pickup, because this list is a snapshot and the ground moves:

- E-2029 dropped the channel tables, and E-1489 and E-1491 ('Port channel DB
  access', 'Port suggestions DB access') are both obsolete for the same reason.
  So E-912's conversation and message half may have no subject left. Check.
- Sessions are deliberately machine-local runtime state today, and several
  schema comments say so ('session_tasks is live-only session state and is not
  rebuilt from the ledger'). Emitting session events changes that premise, so
  E-910's half is a design question, not just wiring. See E-799's analysis.
- E-1035 (focus events failing the session_id FK on replay) is downstream of
  the same gap and has been folded into E-1041.

## From the description

the implementor determines which entities still apply and gets user approval on that scope before building.

Files: config.go (EndlessConfig struct + RootConfig() marker), merge.go (per-field Merge() with semantics from the plan: per-key checks merge, layerable tracking, etc.), normalize.go (defaults; move defaultCheckEnabled from internal/monitor/checks.go here), errors.go (doterr sentinels), load.go (Load(projectPath) wrapping cfgstore.LoadDefaultConfig[EndlessConfig, *EndlessConfig] with ConfigSlug=endless, ConfigFile=config.json).

Struct must include EVERY current field from both ~/.config/endless/config.json (roots, scan_interval, ignore, ownership, node_id, checks) and per-project .endless/config.json (name, label, description, language, status, dependencies, documents, tracking) with JSON tags identical to today so existing files keep loading.

fields.title: Make Python config readers match Go merge rules
fields.description: Make Python config readers honor Go's layered config merge rules, either by reimplementing them or by calling a Go command that returns merged values.
fields.notes:
Follow-up to E-949 (NOT a child).

Spec for Python parity lives in internal/config/README.md (to be written under E-949).
fields.context:
Python has 7+ readers in src/endless/config.py, event_bridge.py, register.py, reconcile.py plus tests, all using direct json.load.

They currently work for the unchanged-config case but will diverge from Go's merge rules for any layered field (today: checks and tracking).

Two viable paths: (a) reimplement the Go merge semantics in Python config.py (gross duplication, fragile); (b) move Python to call a Go shim like 'endless config get <key>' that runs Go's loader and returns the merged value.

Path (b) aligns with the broader E-799 / E-894 direction of Go owning data reads.

Discuss before implementing.

fields.title: Add general-purpose task relation CLI
fields.description: Add creation-time relation flags to task add and decision add, a general relate and unrelate command, full relations in task show, and reverse-lookup filters on list commands.
fields.notes:
Sibling to E-852 (which shipped narrow blocks/blocked-by support).

vocabulary lock is in E-958 and blocks implementation.
fields.analysis:
Sibling to E-852 (which shipped narrow blocks/blocked-by support). Broader scope: make all task_deps relations first-class via CLI rather than requiring manual SQL or text references in descriptions. Punch list (vocabulary decision in E-958, blocking implementation):
1. At-creation flags on endless task add: --blocks <id>, --blocked-by <id>, --relates-to <id> [--rel-type <type>]
2. At-creation flags on endless decision add: --about <task-id> (default dep_type=informs), --decides <task-id> (alternate)
3. General-purpose primitive: endless task relate <source> --to <target> --type <type>; endless task unrelate <source> --to <target> [--type <type>]; endless task block becomes thin wrapper for relate --type blocks
4. Discoverability: endless task show <id> displays ALL relations grouped by type (not just blocks/replaces, which is today's behavior and the reason text-based references slip through unnoticed); endless decision show <id> displays what it links to
5. Expand or sibling-rename endless task deps: either show all relations or add endless task relations <id>; both with --type <type> filter
6. Reverse lookups: endless task list --related-to <id> [--rel-type <type>]; endless decision list --about <task-id>
Schema accepts any dep_type string (CHECK constraints removed), so no migration needed. Implementation order: settle vocabulary first (blocked on E-958), then ship at-creation flags + show-all-relations together (highest impact), then primitive + reverse lookups.

## From the description

Schema accepts any dep_type so no migration is needed;

Punch list and ordering rationale are in the analysis field.

(3) endless task update: do not touch description when updating other fields; require explicit confirmation when clearing. (4) Display fallback in task show / decision show: when description is NULL, render an excerpt of text or '(no description, see text)' rather than blank.

No schema change.

Workstream 2 of E-968.

Project-scoped with global fallback.

New CLI: 'endless phrase {add,list,disable,enable,remove}' with --match and --case-sensitive flags. Seeds: pivot triggers (actually, wait, by the way, ..., plus PIVOT case-sensitive); verbs from current _TITLE_VERBS in src/endless/task_cmd.py; actions from hardcoded regexes in cmd/endless-hook/claude.go. Naming convention: kebab-case for kind values (user-typed at CLI), snake_case for column names. Plan: .endless/plans/E-970.md.

fields.title: Add per-session git worktrees and a topic-drift gate
fields.description: Add git worktrees per session and per task, with single ownership and a clean main to land into, plus a gate that catches topic drift between sessions.
fields.notes:
## Justification

Pre-epic-era umbrella: E-968 workstream 3 with 14+ children that land individually; epics did not exist when filed (2026-04). Retyped per review.

## From the description

Workstream 3 of E-968.

Blocked by E-969 (plan-bearing detection), E-970 (phrase storage), E-972 (project resolution).
fields.analysis:
Two flavors: per-session worktrees (auto-created on session start, removed on session end) and dedicated task worktrees (for plan-bearing tasks; persist across sessions). Rust-style ownership: at most one owner at a time, transferable via .endless/worktree.lock (atomic O_EXCL claim, stale via kill -0, released on SessionEnd). Main = sacred clean integration target; 'endless worktree land' refuses dirty main. Behavioral gate: UserPromptSubmit hook injects active-task system reminder (Layer 1) plus deterministic phrase match against E-970's pivot kind (Layer 2); PIVOT word as deliberate user override; gate clearance via task add or task start (CLI verb required, not chat ack).

Plan: .endless/plans/E-971.md.

fields.title: Add a --decision flag to task add and update
fields.description: Add a --decision flag to task add and task update that creates a paired decision holding the rationale and links it to the task in one step.

Compressing that into one CLI invocation removes the friction that causes rationale to get lost in commit messages or chat instead of the task DB.

Acceptance: 'endless task update E-X --status verify --decision "smoke tested locally"' creates a decision task, links it to E-X, and records the rationale in one shot.

fields.description: Prune plan snapshots not attached to a task, keeping 30 days and 100MB by default, with a command run opportunistically rather than by a daemon.
fields.notes: Once E-969 ships eager plan snapshots to .endless/plans/snapshots/,
fields.analysis:
Once E-969 ships eager plan snapshots to .endless/plans/snapshots/, this task adds the prune mechanism.

Policy:
- Snapshots whose content was attached to a task end up copied to .endless/plans/<task-id>.md, so the snapshot itself is redundant after attach (provenance lives at the task's file).
- Keep for N days (default 30, configurable): unattached snapshots.
- Hard cap (default 100MB, configurable): oldest-first eviction.

CLI: 'endless plan snapshots prune [--days N] [--max-size MB] [--dry-run]'. Idempotent. Surface count and bytes freed. Triggered opportunistically (on 'endless plan snapshots' invocations) or via explicit prune call. No background daemon.

## From the description

Defaults: 30-day retention for unattached snapshots, 100MB hard cap with oldest-first eviction.

Snapshots whose content was attached to a task are redundant after attach (provenance lives at the task's plan file).

fields.title: Add a command to cd into another session's worktree
fields.description: Add endless session cd, which prints the working directory or worktree of a sibling Claude session so a shell function can switch a non-Claude pane there.
fields.analysis:
Primary use case (short term): from a tmux pane that is NOT the Claude pane, get into the cwd / worktree of the Claude session running in a sibling pane so you can run tests, inspect state, or just look around without polluting Claude's working directory.

Resolution rules (in order):
1. Explicit: endless session cd <endless-id> — look up the companion file by endless_session_id, cd to its cwd (or worktree_path if set).
2. Tmux sibling: in tmux with a single sibling Claude pane, auto-resolve to that one. Multiple siblings → list and require disambiguation.
3. Otherwise: error with the list of known companion files so the user can retry with an explicit id.

Implementation notes:
- A child process cannot change its parent shell's cwd. The command therefore prints the target path to stdout and the user wraps it in a shell function (e.g. escd() { cd "$(endless session cd "$@")"; }). Document the function; consider shipping an 'endless shell-init' that prints it.
- Alternative for tmux: when invoked under tmux, optionally tmux send-keys a cd into the calling pane. Cleaner UX but more magic; default off behind a flag.
- Reads .endless/sessions/claude-*.json companion files (E-989). No DB read on the hot path.

Verification:
- Two panes, two sessions, two worktrees: from a third pane, 'endless session cd <id1>' lands in worktree 1; same for id2.
- One Claude pane in tmux: 'endless session cd' (no arg) resolves automatically.
- Two Claude panes, no arg: prints disambiguation list, exits non-zero.
- No tmux, no arg: errors with companion-file list.

Out of scope:
- Auto-cd on session start.
- Cross-window tmux discovery (sibling = same tmux window only, for v1).

## From the description

Resolution rules: explicit endless-id, single tmux sibling auto-resolve, or error with companion-file list. A child process cannot change its parent's cwd, so the command prints the target path and the user wraps it in a shell function (escd). Reads .endless/sessions/claude-*.json (E-989), no DB hot path.

fields.title: Add endless session show for one session's details
fields.description: Add endless session show to display one session's bound task, worktree, start time, message count and last summary, defaulting to the current session.
fields.context: Today there is no concise way to see what a session is, what task it's bound to, where its worktree lives, when it started, and how many messages it has. session list is global and noisy; session history dumps messages.
fields.analysis:
Today there is no concise way to see 'what is this session, what task is it bound to, where is its worktree, when did it start, how many messages.' 'session list' is global and noisy; 'session history' dumps messages. We need a focused per-session detail command — and crucially, one that defaults to the current session without requiring the user to look up a cryptic UUID prefix.

Behavior:
- 'endless session show' (no arg) → resolve current session via the companion file (E-989). In tmux, 'current' means the Claude pane in this window if there is exactly one, else error and list candidates. Outside tmux, 'current' means the companion file whose pid matches a claude ancestor of the calling shell — fall back to error if ambiguous.
- 'endless session show <id>' → explicit lookup by endless integer id or by Claude UUID prefix.

Output (text mode):
- Endless id, Claude UUID, project, state, started_at, last_activity, message count
- Bound task (id + title) if one is active
- Worktree path + branch + dirty/clean if a worktree is bound
- Most recent summary, flattened to one line (we already do this for 'session list')

Add --json for scripting.

Verification:
- From inside a Claude pane: 'endless session show' returns its own session.
- From a sibling pane in tmux: 'endless session show' returns the Claude session in this tmux window.
- Two Claude panes in window: errors with disambiguation list.
- Explicit id always works regardless of context.

## From the description

Output: id, project, state, started_at, last_activity, message count, bound task, worktree path/branch/cleanliness, last summary. --json for scripting.

fields.title: Refactor file-path CLI flags to a --xxx-file convention
fields.description: Refactor CLI flags across endless so any flag taking a file path is named --xxx-file and the bare --xxx flag takes inline content, cutting over in one step.
fields.context: Today some flags carry inline values (--description <text>) and others carry file paths despite the flag name implying inline content (--text <file>, --prompt <file>).
fields.analysis:
Today the CLI's content flags are inconsistent three different ways for the same kind of
(multi-line) content:

- `--text` takes a FILE PATH (dest `text_file`) but the name reads like inline content.
- `--analysis` takes inline content OR a path via `@file` magic (added by E-1329).
- `--outcome` / `--description` take inline content only.

This forces the user to remember which flag means which, and it has already produced a latent
bug: the research handoff template instructs `endless task update … --outcome <file>`, but
`--outcome` has no file form, so the literal path is stored as the outcome text.

## Decision (locked with Mike 2026-06-20)

- Every **long-form content flag** gets BOTH forms: bare `--xxx` carries **inline** content,
  `--xxx-file` carries a **file path**. Applies to: **text, analysis, outcome, description**.
- **justification** and **reason** stay **inline-only** (typically short) — a deliberate
  partial-consistency exception, not an oversight.
- **Remove the `@file` magic** on `--analysis` (E-1329, cli.py); `--analysis-file`
  replaces it. One mechanism, no magic. (No auto-detect of path-vs-inline — brittleness
  outweighs convenience.)
- **Hard cutover**, no alias / migration window (pre-1.0, move-fast, no-legacy).

## Consequence to watch

`--text` today IS the file-path flag, so the change INVERTS it: `--text` becomes inline and
`--text-file` becomes the path form. Every existing `--text <path>` call site (code, templates,
docs, tests) must become `--text-file <path>`.

## Coordination (not blockers)

- E-1000 (text→plan rename): whichever name survives, the `--xxx`/`--xxx-file` split applies.
- E-1554 (adds `--notes`): should follow this convention when it lands.
- Independent of the field-separation design (E-999); applies to whichever flag names survive.
- Origin: E-989 finalization.

## From the description

Apply uniformly across all endless commands.

Endless is pre-1.0 and 'move fast' applies; recommend hard cutover in one shot rather than a migration window.

Verification, surface area, and decisions on auto-detect are in the analysis field.

fields.title: Fix plan-file mirror landing in main from a worktree
fields.description: Fix endless task update --text run inside a worktree so the per-task plan file is written to that worktree instead of the main checkout.
fields.context:
Bug surfaced during E-957 implementation.

Today _project_root_for_task() reads the project's path from the projects table, which is fixed at registration time and points at main.
fields.analysis:
Bug surfaced during E-957 implementation (noted in .endless/plans/E-968.md, W1 section, 2026-04-29 addendum).

When 'endless task update --text' runs from inside a git worktree of the project, the per-task plan-file mirror lands in main's checkout, not the worktree's. Today _project_root_for_task() (src/endless/task_cmd.py, added by E-969) reads the project's path from the projects table — which is fixed at registration time and points at main. From inside a worktree, the file ends up invisible to the worktree's git history until manually copied.

Resolution rule (from the plan):
1. If cwd is inside a registered project's main checkout → return that path (current behavior).
2. If cwd is inside a git worktree of a registered project (detect via 'git rev-parse --git-common-dir' matching the project's .git directory) → return the worktree's root path, NOT main.
3. If neither applies → fall back to DB-stored path with a warning.

Critical file: src/endless/task_cmd.py — _project_root_for_task() (added by E-969).

Verification: from inside a worktree, run 'endless task update E-X --text <path>'. Confirm .endless/plans/E-X.md appears in the worktree's checkout, not main's.

## From the description

Resolution rule: detect cwd-in-worktree via 'git rev-parse --git-common-dir', return the worktree's root in that case. Critical file: src/endless/task_cmd.py.
